citation: Wright, H., Carr, D., Wiese, J., Stokes, L., Runge, J., Dorsett, R., Heal, J., & Anders, J. (2020). URLEY (Using Research Tools to Improve Language in the Early Years): Evaluation report. London: Education Endowment Foundation. (Independent evaluators: National Institute of Economic and Social Research [NIESR] and the Behavioural Insights Team [BIT].)
report_number: EEF project: URLEY (Using Research Tools to Improve Language in the Early Years), 2020
design: School/setting-level two-armed cluster RCT (efficacy trial), business-as-usual control. UK (West Midlands, Liverpool, Manchester). 122 schools recruited; 120 schools randomised (62 intervention, ~58 control) with 2,535 children; primary-outcome analysis sample n=1,978 children (985 intervention; 993 control) across the 120 schools. URLEY is an evidence-based teacher professional development programme for Nursery and Reception teachers (children ages 3-5; pre-kindergarten / early years), centred on evidence-based language-learning principles plus use of the Environment Rating Scales (ERS) as research tools, delivered over six training days + mentoring (6x8 + 17.5 = 65.5 intended hours). Outcomes: primary = composite child language skill score (BPVS + RAPT info + RAPT grammar + CELF Sentence Structure); secondary child outcomes = the four language subscales, ASBI social-behavioural scales, and ERS quality-of-provision (teacher practice) measures. Pre-test Oct-Dec 2016; post-test Jun-Jul 2018. Delivered by URLEY team (University of Oxford / external provider); funded by EEF.
problems: Single TPD arm (URLEY) vs business-as-usual control, mapped to registry row_id 141. Identification: the registry 'Wright et al. 2020' (School RCT, Unpublished, Pre-k, Average/High SES, (P)CK, Long, External trainer) matches the EEF URLEY evaluation report authored by H. Wright et al. (2020); this was cross-confirmed because both Sims et al. (RER) and the EEF teacher-professional-development systematic review cite it as 'Wright, H. et al. (2020). URLEY Evaluation Report. Education Endowment Foundation' and code it as UK / early years-pre-kindergarten / English-language-literacy / 120 units randomised / low-stakes standardised exam. The headline child-achievement contrasts are the language outcomes (all map to Reading per the early-literacy/language->Reading rule). The primary outcome (composite language) is already standardised to mean 0, SD 1, so the impact estimate is directly in SD units and the report labels it Hedges' g = -0.08 (95% CI -0.19, 0.03), p=0.15 (Table 1 exec summary; Table 11/12, p.32-33). Effect sizes are computed per the SAP as Hedges' g = regression coefficient relative to total unadjusted outcome variance. The primary model is a school-level cluster RCT analysed with OLS controlling for the SCHOOL-AVERAGE pre-test composite score (individual-level pre-test was not used in the primary model due to pre-test data-collection issues) plus stratum dummies (FSM-median, location, batch); inference uses school-clustered SEs (Stata cluster option). Therefore pretest_adjusted=true and cluster_adjusted=true (clustering handled by the model). n_clusters=120 (schools randomised; ERS-only models used 117 schools). Realised ICC of the primary outcome = 0.13 (Table 7, p.~24). impact_se left null where the report only gives the g-scale 95% CI; g_se/g_var below are derived from the reported 95% CIs (g_se = (CI_hi - CI_lo)/(2*1.96)). J small-sample correction ~1.000 (df very large, ~1,978 children). Four language subscales (BPVS, RAPT Info, RAPT Grammar, CELF Sentence Structure; Table 13, p.34) are secondary components of the composite -> outcome_role=subscale, is_full_sample=true. The composite-language result for the FSM-eligible subgroup (Table 16, p.~36) is a pre-specified non-randomised subset -> outcome_role=subgroup, is_full_sample=false. EXCLUDED outcomes per spec: ERS quality-of-provision scores (Table 15: composite ERS g=0.69, ECERS-3 g=0.58, ECERS-E literacy g=0.62, SSTEW g=0.52) are TEACHER-PRACTICE / classroom-quality outcomes, not student achievement; ASBI scales are social-behavioural, not academic achievement. All language (achievement) effects are small, negative, and non-significant after multiple-comparison adjustment (CELF was nominally significant but not after Benjamini-Hochberg); headline ~1 month less progress, EEF security 1/5 padlocks due to attrition (22%).

effect_sizes.g_method: Report's Hedges' g (Table 1 exec summary; Table 11, p.32). Composite outcome is standardised to mean 0/SD 1, so the cluster-adjusted, school-average-pretest-adjusted OLS treatment coefficient is already in SD units = g = -0.08 (adjusted difference in means -0.081, Table 12). g_se/g_var derived from reported 95% CI (-0.19, 0.03): g_se=(0.03-(-0.19))/(2*1.96)=0.05612; g_var=g_se^2=0.003150. sd_t/sd_c from Table 12 variances (1.088 and 0.913 -> SD 1.043 and 0.955; pooled var 1.000).
effect_sizes.page_ref: p.6 Table 1 (exec summary); p.32 Table 11; p.33 Table 12; analysis model p.19-20; ICC p.24 Table 7
effect_sizes.notes: PRIMARY confirmatory child-achievement outcome. Early literacy/language -> Reading. ~ -1 month progress, p=0.15, not statistically significant. Model controls for school-average pre-test composite (individual pre-test omitted from primary model) and stratum dummies; SEs clustered at school level so clustering is accounted for.
